# Nimlet

> Nimlet is a lightweight, self-hosted, HTTP-first messaging backend for connecting people, applications, devices, services and AI agents. It provides authentication, room-level authorization, persistent events and recoverable synchronization without requiring a full messaging platform.

Canonical site: https://thiagoribeiro.github.io/nimlet/
GitHub repository: https://github.com/thiagoribeiro/nimlet
License: Apache-2.0

## What it provides

- Authenticated participants: users, devices, sessions and service identities; the server derives the sender from the authenticated session.
- Rooms and permissions: memberships, roles, and authorization for reading and publishing events.
- Persistent communication: append-only room events in PostgreSQL, idempotent sends, paginated history.
- Reconnect-friendly sync: incremental `/sync` over plain HTTP with long polling and opaque cursors; clients recover missed events after disconnecting.
- AppServices: namespace-scoped bridges for bots, AI agents and external systems.
- Namespaces: several independent applications isolated in one deployment.
- Optional media (filesystem or S3-compatible) and Android push notifications.

## Where it fits

- An embedded chat feature in an app or small SaaS.
- A persistent conversation between users and an external AI agent, independent of the LLM or agent framework.
- Commands and replies between a companion app and a connected device, with offline catch-up.
- Bots and integrations that join the same rooms as people.

## What it is not

Not a Matrix homeserver or federation protocol, not a Slack/Mattermost/Rocket.Chat replacement, not a general-purpose message broker, not an LLM agent framework or workflow engine, not a WebSocket-first realtime server, and not an end-to-end encrypted messenger.

## Stack

Go server; PostgreSQL is the source of truth (migrations run at startup); Redis Pub/Sub only wakes `/sync` across instances (latency, not correctness); HMAC-signed opaque bearer tokens.

## Measured (docs/benchmarks.md)

- One instance on 2 cores sustains 2,500 msg/s into rooms of 20 (50k deliveries/s) at delivery p99 under 500 ms.
- Adding and removing instances, killing an instance, and restarting Redis or Postgres under load lost, duplicated or reordered nothing across 78M checked deliveries.
